mechanisms: Arena invocation timing is thread-local opt-in; ordinary Sequence timing remains unchanged. Disable four timing events, terminal synchronize, and elapsed-event synchronization per invocation without removing dispatch validation.

Explicit checked DOOP output(reserve_previous) advice uses the arena last validated row count as an initial capacity only; full metadata, sticky failure checks, bounded writes and overflow replay precede publication. Count/reserve/bounded behavior is unchanged.
Injective layout permutations use unsafe sort_known_unique: radix sort plus copy/gather, no unique compaction/count readback. Arbitrary inputs and admission retain deduplication.

timings.sampling: One untraced and one profiled execution per version; timings are observations, not confidence intervals. Historic 3.672471s is not used as the paired baseline.

formal_rules.name: GPU-Arena-Timing
formal_rules.text: For an arena invocation, disabled timing permits omission only of terminal timing events, their elapsed-time publication, and the redundant terminal stream fence. All dispatch count and failure validation remains before publication; same-stream ordering and retained owners preserve validity. Enabled timing restores synchronizing measurements without changing the candidate bag.

formal_rules.name: GPU-ReservePrevious
formal_rules.text: The explicitly recorded reserve_previous protocol is realized only by an arena terminal. The last validated count, initially zero, is an initial capacity hint, not a bound. Every attempt counts all candidates and writes only within capacity; sticky arithmetic/fold failure aborts. If the count exceeds capacity, discard the unpublished attempt and replay the unchanged invocation snapshot at the required capacity. Publish and remember only a fully validated initialized prefix; never admit a truncated batch.

formal_rules.name: DL-SortKnownUnique
formal_rules.text: An injective column permutation of an initialized unique run remains unique and preserves its known cardinality. Sorting that prefix produces a sorted unique run of the same length without compaction or a count readback. Other arbitrary inputs still require unique canonicalization.

disjoint_internal_kernel_gap_partition.method: Intersect each traced CUDA API interval with the complement of the kernel interval union, restricted to first kernel start through last kernel end. Assign each intersected interval to exactly one API category; the remainder is no-recorded-CUDA-API time. All observed CUDA API records use one thread and are nonoverlapping: summed API duration equals its union (2,594,547,754 ns).
interpretation: This is a disjoint partition of the 1.829632383 s internal kernel-gap interval set, not of the 3.897107 s evaluation. It excludes all kernel-overlapping API time and time before first/after last kernel.
DtoH metadata plus compaction-count API residence accounts for 176,482,920 ns of internal gaps, not the 1.914779751 s summed residence of those APIs.

No-recorded-CUDA-API is a residual, not measured CPU-on-core time: it can include host computation, wrapper/allocation/cache work outside traced CUDA APIs, untraced driver work, scheduling, profiler overhead and GPU memory activity.
API attribution reports where the host thread resides while no kernel executes, not causality or avoidable overhead; kernels can be absent because memory activity is executing.

Final dispatch synchronization versus optional timing cannot be identified without call stacks or annotations. Stream and event synchronization are reported separately; event_management includes create/record/query/destroy and is not assumed to be optional timing. Terminal synchronization after the last kernel is outside this partition.

The reproducible sweep query assumes globally unique correlation IDs and nonoverlapping CUDA API intervals on one thread, both observed in this before report. Recheck these preconditions before applying to a multithreaded after report.
disjoint_internal_kernel_gap_partition.reproducible_sql:
WITH kernels AS (
 SELECT k.start,k.end,k.correlationId,s.value name FROM CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_KERNEL k JOIN StringIds s ON s.id=k.shortName
), submission_events AS (
 SELECT correlationId,'kernel' kind,name,0 bytes FROM kernels
 UNION ALL SELECT correlationId,'dtoh','',bytes FROM CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_MEMCPY WHERE copyKind=2
), preceding AS (
 SELECT *,LAG(kind) OVER (ORDER BY correlationId) prior_kind,LAG(name) OVER (ORDER BY correlationId) prior_name FROM submission_events
), dtoh_protocol AS (
 SELECT correlationId,CASE WHEN prior_kind='kernel' AND prior_name LIKE '__cq_sequence_dispatch_%' THEN 'dtoh_metadata'
 WHEN bytes=8 AND prior_kind='kernel' AND prior_name LIKE 'scatter_selected%' THEN 'dtoh_compaction_count'
 ELSE 'dtoh_payload_other' END category FROM preceding WHERE kind='dtoh'
), api AS (
 SELECT r.start,r.end,r.correlationId,CASE
 WHEN s.value='cuMemcpyDtoHAsync_v2' THEN d.category
 WHEN s.value='cuStreamSynchronize' THEN 'stream_synchronize'
 WHEN s.value='cuEventSynchronize' THEN 'event_synchronize'
 WHEN s.value IN ('cuEventCreate','cuEventRecord','cuEventDestroy_v2','cuEventQuery','cuEventElapsedTime') THEN 'event_management'
 WHEN s.value IN ('cuMemAllocAsync','cuMemAlloc_v2','cuMemAllocHost_v2') THEN 'allocation'
 WHEN s.value IN ('cuMemFreeAsync','cuMemFree_v2','cuMemFreeHost') THEN 'free'
 WHEN s.value LIKE 'cuMemset%' THEN 'memset'
 WHEN s.value='cuLaunchKernel' THEN 'launch'
 WHEN s.value='cuMemcpyHtoDAsync_v2' THEN 'upload'
 WHEN s.value='cuMemcpyDtoDAsync_v2' THEN 'device_to_device_copy'
 WHEN s.value='cuModuleLoadData' THEN 'module_load'
 ELSE 'other_api' END category
 FROM CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_RUNTIME r JOIN StringIds s ON s.id=r.nameId LEFT JOIN dtoh_protocol d ON d.correlationId=r.correlationId
), boundaries AS (
 SELECT start t,correlationId+1 api_id,0 kernel FROM api UNION ALL SELECT end,-(correlationId+1),0 FROM api
 UNION ALL SELECT start,0,1 FROM kernels UNION ALL SELECT end,0,-1 FROM kernels
), grouped AS (
 SELECT t,SUM(api_id) api_id,SUM(kernel) kernel FROM boundaries GROUP BY t
), segments AS (
 SELECT t,LEAD(t) OVER (ORDER BY t) next_t,SUM(api_id) OVER (ORDER BY t) active_api,SUM(kernel) OVER (ORDER BY t) active_kernel FROM grouped
), bounds AS (
 SELECT MIN(start) first_kernel,MAX(end) last_kernel FROM kernels
)
SELECT COALESCE(a.category,'no_recorded_cuda_api') category,SUM(g.next_t-g.t) gap_duration_ns,
 COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN g.active_api<>0 THEN g.active_api END) api_calls_intersecting_gaps
FROM segments g CROSS JOIN bounds b LEFT JOIN api a ON a.correlationId=g.active_api-1
WHERE g.active_kernel=0 AND g.t>=b.first_kernel AND g.next_t<=b.last_kernel
GROUP BY category ORDER BY gap_duration_ns DESC
